CAT.rationale: Caterpillar's fundamental health is strong with excellent revenue growth (+22.2% YoY in Q1 2026) and robust EPS growth (+30.2% YoY), but the valuation has become extremely stretched. The stock trades at a P/E of 46.4x versus a historical range of 19.4-52.6x over the past year, and a P/B of 23.4x versus a range of 10.7-26.6x. This represents a massive premium to its own history. The company faces significant headwinds including $2.2-2.4B in projected tariff costs for 2026, margin contraction in Resource Industries (39% YoY profit decline), and rising manufacturing costs. Michael Burry has initiated a short position citing unsustainable valuation. The stock has rallied 150% over 12 months, creating extreme multiple compression risk. While the Q2 earnings beat is a near-term positive, the stock is priced for perfection with a P/E of 46x for a cyclical industrial company, making it extremely vulnerable to any slowdown in AI data center spending or macroeconomic weakness.
